note: The United Kingdom: Irish citizens may live and work freely under the Common Travel Area. Everyone else offered work as a creative worker (an actor, a dancer, a musician) needs the Temporary Work – Creative Worker visa, on a licensed sponsor's certificate of sponsorship. A visitor may undertake permitted paid engagements (an artist, entertainer or musician invited to perform) completed within 30 days of entering, taken as 30 days worked without the visa (the invitation and the visitor's other conditions aren't modelled; a non-visa national's entry under the creative worker concession isn't modelled apart).

sources.title: GOV.UK, Creative Worker visa (Temporary Work): Overview
sources.said: You must apply for a Temporary Work - Creative Worker visa if: you’ve been offered work in the UK as a creative worker ... A creative worker is someone who works in the creative industries, for example an actor, dancer, musician or film crew member. ... You need to have a certificate of sponsorship from a licensed sponsor before you can apply to come to the UK to work.

sources.title: GOV.UK, Immigration Rules Appendix Visitor: Permitted Activities, PA 19
sources.said: Permitted Paid Engagements PA 19. A Visitor may undertake the permitted paid engagements in V 13.3, providing they are completed within 30 days of the Visitor’s entry to the UK, and the requirements of V 13.1. to V 13.2. are met.

sources.title: GOV.UK, Common Travel Area guidance
sources.said: Under the CTA , British and Irish citizens can move freely and reside in either jurisdiction and enjoy associated rights and privileges, including the right to work, study and vote in certain elections
